messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] SNP Associations for F2
messages.body_plain:
Similar to summary() in R/qtl1, find_peaks() has the default of just return in the largest LOD score on each chromosome. You can try to use the 'peakdrop' argument to get at secondary peaks on a chromosome, but I understand you're wanting to look at the results in more detail.

The output of scan1() is a matrix of LOD scores, with rows being positions and columns being phenotypes. You could try just viewing the rows the exceed a particular value.

This would print all of the rows where the maximum LOD score in that row is > 4:

  max_by_row <- apply(my_scan1_output, 1, max)
  my_scan1_output[ max_by_row > 4, ]

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl2 version 0.14
messages.body_plain:
I've just released a new version of R/qtl2 (ver 0.14). To update, use:

    update.packages(ask=FALSE, repos="https://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

Here are the main changes <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md>; nothing really big:

New features

Added function clean_genoprob() which cleans genotype probabilities by setting small values to 0 and, for genotype columns where the maximum value is not large, setting all values to 0. This is intended to help with the problem of unstable estimates of genotype effects in scan1coef() and fit1() when there's a genotype that is largely absent.

Added function compare_maps() for comparing marker order between two marker maps.

Revised the order of arguments in reduce_markers() to match pick_marker_subset(), because I like the latter better. Removed the function pick_marker_subset() because it's identical to reduce_markers(). (Seriously, I implemented the same thing twice.)
 <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/master/NEWS.md#minor-changes>Minor changes

plot_coef() now uses a named lodcolumn argument, if provided, to subset scan1_output, if that's provided.

In the documentation for scan1coef(), scan1blup(), and fit1(), revised the suggested contrasts for getting additive and dominance effects in an intercross.
Karl Broman | kbroman.org <http://kbroman.org>

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

In attempting to use covariates in est_herit(), I get the following error:

> est_herit(cross$pheno, k_simple, covar)

Error in est_herit(cross$pheno, k_simple, covar) :

Removing covar and running est_herit() without it seems to work fine.

I think the issue is from get_common_ids():

>get_common_ids(cross$pheno, covar, complete.cases = T)
character(0)

covar, in this case, is a 192 X 4 matrix, with the correct samples IDs as rownames. If I use a matrix with a single covariate, and set names() to rownames(covar), it seems to work fine. Any suggestions for setting names for a multi-column matrix?

Thanks,
Basel

messages.subject: Re: maxmarg() minprob for Diversity Outbred mice
messages.subject_clean: maxmarg() minprob for Diversity Outbred mice
messages.body_plain:
> is there a guideline for the minimum probability for a call for Diversity Outbred mice? Or should I just keep the default 0.95?

There's no simple answer to this question. A higher value will mean more NAs in the output. A smaller value will mean fewer NAs but more possible errors.
The appropriate position in that trade-off depends on what you're trying to do.

karl
